summary: The Returning Unspent COVID Funds Act cancels certain unused funds that were originally provided to address COVID-19. These canceled funds must be kept in the Treasury specifically to reduce the national deficit, though the President may waive this cancellation for specific accounts or programs by notifying Congress within 60 days of the bill's enactment.

affected_groups.effect: These programs will lose their remaining unobligated funds unless the President issues a waiver.
affected_groups.group: Federal programs with unspent COVID-19 funds

key_provisions: Cancels unobligated balances of funds from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021.
Cancels unobligated balances from Divisions M and N of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021.
Cancels unobligated balances from the Paycheck Protection Program and Health Care Enhancement Act.
Cancels unobligated balances from the CARES Act, the Families First Coronavirus Response Act, and the Coronavirus Preparedness and Response Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2020.
Requires all canceled funds to remain in the general fund of the Treasury solely for deficit reduction.
Allows the President to waive the cancellation for an account or program by submitting a notice to the House Budget Committee and the Senate Finance Committee within 60 days.
missing_information: The total amount of unobligated COVID-19 funds that will be rescinded.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Returning Unspent COVID Funds Act cancels certain unused funds that were originally provided to address COVID-19. These canceled funds must be kept in the Treasury specifically to reduce the national deficit, though the President may waive this cancellation for specific accounts or programs by notifying Congress within 60 days of the bill's enactment.
summary_detail.significance: This bill impacts federal budgetary accounting by redirecting unused COVID-19 relief monies toward national deficit reduction. The significance level is moderate (score 50), as it affects existing federal accounts across multiple past COVID-19 laws, though the exact total dollar amount of unobligated funds being cancelled is not specified in the text.
